description: We are Team Turtlers, a team from Dhaka, currently working on the "Flame in FireFall" Problem. Our team covers AI, ML, Data Science and Development. If you have prior skills, Do join us.
summary:
AegnyxZero is an interactive, Super Intelligence (SI)-powered dashboard that delivers evidence-first fire safety insights for human spaceflight. Utilizing decades of NASA microgravity combustion data from the PSI and NTRS repositories, AegnyxZero helps mission planners design safer lunar and Martian habitats. Users select atmospheric conditions (e.g., the 30% oxygen, 70 kPa lunar cabin environment) to rank materials by fire risk. 

Unlike generic AI chatbots that hallucinate numbers, AegnyxZero employs a deterministic pure-Python validation engine (V-1 to V-7) to ensure every number is explicitly cited and verified against NASA documents. It also visualizes a "Coverage Map" to highlight experimental data gaps where NASA has never run tests, prioritizing future research. Built with React, FastAPI, and LangGraph, it is a mission-control instrument designed for trust, transparency, and human space exploration.
details:
AegnyxZero solves the challenge of finding, comparing, and interpreting decades of NASA combustion science data.

WHAT IT DOES:

It ranks materials by fire risk under user-selected habitat conditions (O2%, pressure, airflow). If a user selects the "Lunar Habitat" preset (30% O2, 70 kPa), the dashboard instantly ranks materials from Severe to Low risk, showing the exact evidence, page numbers, and quotes from NASA reports for every single metric.

HOW IT WORKS & TOOLS USED:

Built with a React/TypeScript frontend (the "Sphere Instrument" design system), a Python FastAPI backend, LangGraph for AI orchestration, and ChromaDB for vector search. The AI uses a multi-provider gateway (OpenRouter, Groq) but is strictly constrained by a deterministic Validator Engine (V-1 to V-7). The LLM never calculates math; it only explains the data retrieved from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database.

CREATIVITY & IMPACT:

Instead of hiding what it doesn't know, AegnyxZero features a 5x5 "Coverage Map" that exposes the 68% experimental gap where NASA has never tested microgravity fires. It also integrates a "Context & Impact" module, connecting the data to the Apollo 1 and Mir fires, and translating the physics to Earth applications like advanced firefighter gear and water-mist extinguishers.

Note to Judges: The live application is hosted on Vercel (frontend) and Render (backend). Because Render's free tier sleeps after inactivity, the very first load may take 30–45 seconds to wake the backend. Thank you for your patience! The GitHub repository is also linked in the "Other Data" section below.
